title: Why does one line in this chapter refuse to repeat?

beats.narration: This chapter repeats itself word for word. Except once. Can you hear the change?
The lines addressed to the other side are a frozen refrain. Verse three and verse five are the identical sentence, repeated letter for letter. But the speaker's own lines refuse to hold still.

First he says, I do not serve what you serve. Present tense. This moment. Then comes the line that breaks the symmetry. Nor am I one who serves what you have served. That reaches back across the whole past. Their posture is photographed twice, unchanged. His denial moves through time.

One side is pinned to a single unchanging stance. The other side's refusal covers the present and the entire settled past. By the last verse, to you your way and to me mine, the separation is already total. Grammar sealed it.
